question: Does query-independent rejection sampling even pass an optimistic cost screen for client-only token output?
decision: No tuning: uniform, calibration mean and pointwise-max proposals fixed before heldout execution. If all calibrated envelopes fail or cost exceeds V, retire those direct candidates; oracle finite-set optimum is a lower bound only. Positive numeric screening requires a separate complete strict-private-output construction.
limits: Numerical necessary filter only. Logits and normalizers supplied free; no MPC, private exp, hidden candidate row selection, secure random generation, first-success cost, timing or fullLLM benefit. Proposal candidates must be secret or have an explicit changed ideal functionality: public input-independent proposals correlate with final sampled token and cannot automatically be treated as free public randomness for a client-only-output sampler. Empirical calibration envelopes are not all-input certificates. Clipping changes the target law. Sample count fixed, acceptance flags and first-success index must not be revealed. Oracle context envelopes and heldout-minimax proposal are unavailable in a real protocol and are optimistic diagnostics. This is standard rejection sampling, not a novelty claim. Single tiny model; no large-model extrapolation.
